blocks.content: A toleration is applied to a Pod, and it permits, but does not force, that Pod to be scheduled onto a node carrying a matching taint, the completing half of the taints mechanism from the previous topic.

Where a taint lives on a node and repels, a toleration lives on a Pod and grants permission to ignore a specific matching taint, letting that particular Pod land on a node it would otherwise be repelled from.

blocks.alt: Permission granted to one specific Pod, to ignore one specific taint

blocks.content: This is a genuinely important distinction from affinity: a toleration does not attract a Pod to a node, or force it there, it only removes the repulsion. The Pod might still land on a completely different node, tolerating a taint just makes the tainted node one of the eligible options again.

blocks.alt: Permission to be considered there, not a guarantee of actually landing there

blocks.content: 3. The Toleration Must Match the Taint
blocks.text: 3. The Toleration Must Match the Taint

blocks.content: A toleration is not a blanket "ignore all taints" switch, its key, value, and effect have to specifically match the taint it is meant to tolerate, a mismatched toleration simply does nothing for that particular taint.

blocks.alt: A specific match required, not a general-purpose override

blocks.content: It is worth restating the baseline clearly: a tainted node repels Pods by default, and stays that way for every Pod, except the specific ones carrying a matching toleration, this default-closed behavior is deliberate.

blocks.alt: Closed by default, open only for Pods that explicitly opt in

blocks.content: A GPU-requiring workload might carry a toleration matching a taint applied to specialized GPU nodes, letting it, and only it, actually be scheduled there, while every other ordinary Pod continues to be repelled.

blocks.alt: A specialized workload, and only it, permitted onto specialized nodes

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A toleration, applied to a Pod, permits scheduling onto a node with a matching taint, it grants eligibility, it does not force or guarantee placement there.
The toleration's key, value, and effect must specifically match the taint, and everything not explicitly tolerating a taint stays repelled from that node by default.
